title: Namayan
capsule: Namayan was a precolonial polity on the Pasig River in what is now Metro Manila, Philippines, organized as a confederation of barangays under the hereditary house of Lakantagkan. Its territory spanned communities later known as Santa Ana, Pandacan, Mandaluyong, Makati, and Taytay, and it was distinguished from the trade-oriented polities of Tondo and Maynila by its emphasis on fishing, carpentry, and textile production. The last attested ruler, Rajah Kalamayin, is recorded in Spanish Franciscan sources through 1575. Spanish forces under Miguel López de Legazpi absorbed the polity into the Captaincy General of the Philippines in 1571.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is poorly attested; boundaries are reconstructed from early Spanish administrative records and archaeological site distributions at Santa Ana rather than contemporary maps or boundary documents.
